Migrating from simevent 0.1.1

Source: vignettes/migrating.qmd 
library(simevent)

Introduction

simevent 0.1.1’s functions (simEventData(), the preset wrappers such as simSurvData(), sim.generic(), sim.from.data(), alphaSim(), …) have been removed in favour of the sim_model()/simulate_events() API. This vignette shows how to translate code using the old functions. See vignette("simevent") for an introduction to the new API itself.

simevent 0.1.1 Replacement
simEventData(), simSurvData(), simCRdata(), simDisease(), simTreatment(), simStatinData(), sim.generic(), … sim_model() + simulate_events()
alphaSim(), intEffectAlpha() simulate_events(intervene = ) + event_risk()
sim.from.data() sim_model_from_fits()
IntFormatData() format_interval_data()
plotEventData() plot_event_data()

The old functions coded events as integers in Delta; simulate_events() returns the process name in event, and id/time in place of ID/Time.

Translating the Preset Wrappers

simSurvData()

simSurvData()’s default (beta = NULL, i.e. no covariate effects) is two terminal processes, censoring and death, both with eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1. The old call

simSurvData(200)

becomes

model <- sim_model(
  L0 = sim_covariate(function(N) runif(N)),
  A0 = sim_covariate(function(N, L0) rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)),
  censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  death = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1)
)
model_data <- simulate_events(model, n = 200)

simCRdata()

simCRdata() adds a third terminal process (a second competing cause):

beta <- matrix(c(0.5, -1, -0.5, 0.5, 0, 0.5), ncol = 3, nrow = 2)
simCRdata(N = 200, beta = beta)

becomes

model <- sim_model(
  L0 = sim_covariate(function(N) runif(N)),
  A0 = sim_covariate(function(N, L0) rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)),
  censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  cause1 = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  cause2 = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  effects = list(
    sim_effect(censoring ~ L0 + A0, coef = c(0.5, -1)),
    sim_effect(cause1 ~ L0 + A0, coef = c(-0.5, 0.5)),
    sim_effect(cause2 ~ A0, coef = 0.5)
  )
)
model_data <- simulate_events(model, n = 200)

simDisease()

simDisease() has a censoring process, a terminal death process, and a covariate process L that can happen at most once and can itself affect death; a "transient" process with limit = 1:

simDisease(
  N = 5000,
  cens = 1,
  eta = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.1),
  nu = c(1.1, 1.3, 1.1),
  beta_L0_L = 1,
  beta_A0_L = -1.1,
  beta_L_D = 1,
  beta_L0_D = 0
)

becomes

model <- sim_model(
  L0 = sim_covariate(function(N) runif(N)),
  A0 = sim_covariate(function(N, L0) rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)),
  censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  death = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.3, nu = 1.3),
  L = sim_process("transient", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1, limit = 1),
  effects = list(
    sim_effect(L ~ L0, 1),
    sim_effect(L ~ A0, -1.1),
    sim_effect(death ~ L, 1)
  )
)
model_data <- simulate_events(model, n = 5000)

simTreatment()

simTreatment() (with op = 1, the default) adds a second "transient" process, treatment (A), which can itself affect and be affected by the covariate process L. simTreatment() doesn’t declare its own A0, so its translation skips it too: sim_model() has no default covariates.

simTreatment(
  N = 5000,
  beta_L_A = 1,
  beta_L_D = 1,
  beta_A_D = -1,
  beta_A_L = -0.5,
  beta_L0_A = 1,
  eta = rep(0.1, 4),
  nu = rep(1.1, 4),
  cens = 1,
  op = 1
)

becomes

model <- sim_model(
  L0 = sim_covariate(function(N) runif(N)),
  censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  death = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  A = sim_process("transient", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1, limit = 1),
  L = sim_process("transient", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1, limit = 1),
  effects = list(
    sim_effect(death ~ L0, 1),
    sim_effect(A ~ L0, 1),
    sim_effect(L ~ L0, 1),
    sim_effect(death ~ A, -1),
    sim_effect(L ~ A, -0.5),
    sim_effect(death ~ L, 1),
    sim_effect(A ~ L, 1)
  )
)
model_data <- simulate_events(model, n = 5000)

simStatinData()

simStatinData() mainly demonstrates non-default baseline covariate generators. sim_covariate() reproduces this directly, with no forced covariate names to work around:

set.seed(1405)
model <- sim_model(
  L0 = sim_covariate(function(N) rbinom(N, 1, 0.4)),
  A0 = sim_covariate(function(N, L0) pmin(rexp(N, 0.3) + 70, 100)),
  censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.025, nu = 1.1),
  death = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.025, nu = 1.1)
)
model_data <- simulate_events(model, n = 200)
summary(model_data$A0)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   70.00   70.82   71.96   73.14   74.18   85.01

sim.generic()

sim.generic()’s alpha.intervention/baseline.intervention pair is replaced by simulate_events()’s single intervene list: give a process name to scale its eta, or a covariate name to fix it to a constant, as in simulate_events(model, n, intervene = list(death = 0.2, L0 = 1)).

alphaSim() and intEffectAlpha()

alphaSim() and intEffectAlpha() simulate one of the preset settings with the eta of one process multiplied by alpha, and summarise the result as the proportion of individuals experiencing death and the intervened process by time \tau (or the years lost to them before \tau). Take the "Disease" setting with alpha = 0.5:

alphaSim(
  N = 5000,
  eta = rep(0.1, 3),
  nu = rep(1.1, 3),
  alpha = 0.5,
  tau = 5,
  setting = "Disease"
)

becomes a sim_model() of the setting, simulated with intervene = list(L = 0.5) and summarised with event_risk(). alphaSim() switches censoring off by default, so pass cens = 0:

model <- sim_model(
  L0 = sim_covariate(function(N) runif(N)),
  A0 = sim_covariate(function(N, L0) rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)),
  censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  death = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),
  L = sim_process("transient", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1, limit = 1),
  effects = list(
    sim_effect(death ~ L0, 1),
    sim_effect(L ~ L0, 1),
    sim_effect(death ~ L, 1)
  )
)
set.seed(1405)
intervened <- simulate_events(
  model,
  n = 5000,
  cens = 0,
  intervene = list(L = 0.5)
)
event_risk(intervened, model, c("death", "L"), tau = 5)
#>    process   risk
#>     <char>  <num>
#> 1:   death 0.7012
#> 2:       L 0.2538

The remaining arguments map as follows:

  • years_lost = TRUE is event_risk(type = "time_lost").
  • a0 (summarise only individuals with A0 == a0) is by = "A0", which summarises every group at once.
  • intEffectAlpha()’s plot = TRUE is plot_event_data() on the intervened data.

See “Estimating Intervention Effects” in vignette("simevent") for comparing against the run without intervention.

sim.from.data()

sim_model_from_fits() builds a sim_model() from a list of fitted coxph() models (one per process) and the data they were fit to. Unlike sim.from.data(), there’s no sim.parameters list to build:

  • The baseline.summary computed by hand from mean()/sd()/min()/max() is gone: baseline covariates are resampled as whole rows of the data, keeping each covariate’s distribution and the relationships between them.
  • "(region==2)"-style expressions for categorical covariates are replaced by factor columns used directly in the coxph() formula; dummies are named to match coxph()’s own coefficient names ("<variable><level>").

See “Building a sim_model() from Fitted Cox Models” in vignette("simevent") for a worked example.
